data.outcome_summary: This document is an IEA PIRLS 2001 international report (fourth grade reading literacy) that presents descriptive and benchmarked results on reading achievement and extensive contextual indicators (home, school, teacher, and student questionnaires). PIRLS uses an IRT-based scaling approach to place achievement on a common scale (international mean 500, SD 100) and generates five plausible values per student to reflect uncertainty from matrix sampling. The assessment covers two reading purposes (literary experience; acquire and use information) and four comprehension processes, with 98 items across multiple passages and a matrix sampling plan limiting each student to two of eight passages. Sampling is a two-stage stratified cluster design (schools, then intact classrooms), and jackknife procedures are used to estimate standard errors. International benchmarks correspond to the 90th, 75th, 50th, and 25th percentiles of the international distribution, with sampling weights applied so each country contributes proportionally to its target population.
